set: production nine — built, moved, handed over
arrangement: 3x3 checkerboard; a card never touches a card

posts.why: The set opens inside the hall: an A-frame with its cladding half done and the offcuts still on the floor. Nothing says 'we build this ourselves' like a frame nobody tidied for the camera.
The claim of the whole set, in the words /factory/ already uses. Forest ground, cream type — the pairing the launch nine proved.
A kitchen whose worktop still wears its protective film. The photograph does the arguing: fit-out happens in the hall, not on the plot.
The one number that makes road delivery possible, already public on the site. A numeral is where the eye rests between pictures.
The centre tile gets the strongest frame: a unit behind the tow vehicle at dusk, actually moving. The whole set pivots on it.
The delivery promise the site makes on every country page, on the set's one near-black. It reads like method, not marketing.
Two units on tandem-axle trailers in the yard. Pairs with 5: before the road, and on it.
The loudest ground carries the shortest sentence in the set — the three steps between yard and road, in the order they happen.
Two units prepared for a delivery, flags of Türkiye and Azerbaijan on the facade. The duo band keeps the type off the photograph — the picture is the claim, and it needs no help.
